title: BxORM with cborm
body: Building the blog with ColdBox ? cborm is the ColdBox module for the ORM. title: Coming from CFML
body: Many teams arrive at BxORM with an ORM app already written in CFML. Good news: BxORM is designed to be compatible with existing CFML ORM code. Your persistent components, relationships and ORM functions carry over, and a short list of settings and defaults needs attention. title: Criteria queries
body: Filters like { name : "Ann" } only go so far. The blog needs searches like "published posts by Ann, tagged orm, newest first, page 2". That is a job for criteria queries : a query you build by chaining methods. posts = entityCriteria( "Post" ) .isTrue( "published" ) .isEq( "author.email", "ann@example.com" ) .order( "createdDate", "desc" ) .list(); entityCriteria( "Post" ) starts a query. title: Errors and observability
body: Things go wrong: a duplicate email, a typo in a property name, a page that suddenly runs forty queries. BxORM is built to make these easy to see and fix. Errors written for humans Every ORM error has a type that starts with orm , and a message that says what happened and how to fix it: orm.entity.notFound: There is no entity named [Usr]. title: Events, soft delete and timestamps
body: Real apps need rules around their data: stamp the edit time, never delete a published post, send an email once a post is really saved. BxORM gives you three tools for this: automatic timestamps, entity events and soft delete. title: HQL, structs and queries
body: Criteria queries cover most needs. When a query is easier to write as text, use HQL , Hibernate's query language. And when you send data out of your app, as JSON or a report, you want plain structs or a query object, not entities. This lesson covers both. title: Inheritance
body: Look at the blog's three entities: each one declares an id , and Post has createdDate and updatedDate . As an app grows, you want those shared pieces in one place. And sometimes one entity really is several kinds of thing: a media item that is either an image or a video. Inheritance handles both. title: Static helpers
body: The functions from the last lesson all start with an entity name: entityLoadByPK( "User", 1 ) . BxORM also adds static helper methods to every entity class at startup, so the same work reads like plain English: ann = User::get( 1 ); bob = User::findWhere( { email : "bob@example.com" } ); total = User::count(); There is no base class to extend and no service to write. title: Transactions and the session
body: You have wrapped every write in transaction {} so far. This lesson explains why, and what happens between loading an entity and the SQL reaching the database. The session Every request (or script run) has an ORM session . It remembers every entity you load or save, so: Loading the same row twice gives you the same object, with one query. title: Welcome to BxORM
body: Most applications keep their data in a relational database: tables, rows and columns. Most application code thinks in objects: a user, a post, a tag. An ORM (object-relational mapper) connects the two. You describe a class once, and the ORM turns rows into objects when you load them and objects into rows when you save them. BxORM is the ORM for BoxLang. It runs on Hibernate 7, the most widely used…

title: Your first entity
